messages:
Elena (Marketing): Dropping an updated approach for the competitive battlecard. Shift from feature lists to 'serving scenarios' + 3 short proof points (latency, unit cost predictability, rollout safety). Uploaded: https://redwood.app/drive/serve-econ-v2 :mag:
David (Field): Love the scenarios idea. Can we add micro-scripts for discovery calls? e.g., customer says 'we're on cloud endpoints' -> quick script to push reliability + cost predictability.
Liam (Sales): Need a one-sentence ROI nugget for discovery: something like 'Dedicated inference reduces unpredictable token cost by removing noisy neighbors + caching benefits.' Keep it sub-25 words.
Nina (Product): Add a small qualifier: 'savings depend on workload pattern and sequence lengths' — we should avoid blanket % claims. Also attach a short note on fallback policies so AEs can explain how we avoid outages without sacrificing latency.
Ivy (Growth): For launch posts, I'm thinking two angles: 1) Technical audience: benchmark blog + reproducible CSV; 2) Exec audience: short case-study style claim about predictable unit cost. We should A/B the CTAs.
Elena (Marketing): Yes. Draft CTAs: "Run a 14-day dedicated trial" and "See benchmark reproducibility". We'll split traffic and measure MQL rate.
bench-bot: New benchmark CSV uploaded by Sam-ops: https://bench.redwood/benchmarks/2026-03-19/dedicated-vs-cloud.csv
David (Field): For objection handling, include 3 succinct lines: developer velocity (hosted API for dev), mid-stage (dedicated for predictable ops), enterprise (private for compliance). 
Liam (Sales): Can someone give me a 2-line micro-script for procurement? They always ask: 'why pay more for dedicated?' I need something crisp.
Nina (Product): Try: 'Cloud endpoints are ideal for experimentation. For production with SLOs, teams pick dedicated inference to control latency tails and per-token economics.'
Ivy (Growth): I'll prep webinar hook: "Live: Failover without user impact — watch region fail then variant fallback in 6 minutes". Short demo + 10m AMA. Landing page draft incoming.
Elena (Marketing): Also proposing a short benchmark explainer card in the battlecard that links out to the running CSV and test notes (seq length, batch config, warm-up). Prevents stale numbers.
David (Field): For scripts, add an optional line: 'If they push cloud vendor performance, ask about p99 tail-latency during peaks.' That usually reveals pain.
Liam (Sales): Great. I'll rehearse the script with the SDRs tomorrow. Can we include a bulleted Objection FAQ in the Card? 4 items tops.
Elena (Marketing): Yes — will draft 4-item FAQ (cost, latency, model quality, security). Nina, can you sanity-check the model-quality line?
Nina (Product): Will do. Suggest: 'We match open-model quality for common tasks; for specialized tasks we support customer model pinning and gradual rollouts.'
Ivy (Growth): Routing idea: tag leads with 'bench_click', 'trial_request', 'compliance' and send to different flows. I'll put pseudo-rules in the doc.
Elena (Marketing): Paste of routing pseudo-rules below:
```
if utm_campaign contains (bench OR benchmark) or click on benchmark link -> tag:bench_click -> assign:solutions-nurture
if form contains (trial OR dedicated trial) -> tag:trial_request -> assign:growth-trial-team
if text contains (private OR vpc OR kms OR compliance) -> tag:enterprise -> assign:enterprise-sdr
```
bench-bot: Reminder: schedule benchmark blog publish window is Friday 10:00 PT.
David (Field): Can someone make a 1-pager for field with the 2-up benchmark link + the 4 FAQ bullets? I'll use for calls and AE handoffs.
Elena (Marketing): I'll assemble v1 by tomorrow morning. Owners recap: Elena -> battlecard + FAQ; Ivy -> webinar landing + routing rules; David -> field one-pager; Nina -> claim caveats; Liam -> SDR rehearsals. Closing thread, will ping for review. :rocket:
